units.text: Scar. Whenever a friendly unit with Scar gains stats, your other Great beasts gain +1 Attack this combat.

how_they_play: Scar wants to survive hits, so it pairs with this batch's damage reducers: a boar given Shell, standing next to a Shoulder bear, or behind a whistle survives more hits and grows from each. Enemy Peck and WIDE boards, normally good against walls, feed it with every small hit.
why_run_it: It turns the damage reducers into scaling, and it punishes swarms that try to chip it down.
scene: Turn 3, you buy Scarred Boar. Turn 6, Old Tusker sits in F2 at 4/12. The enemy's tokens hit it five times for 2: each hit leaves it alive and adds +2/+2, so it ends the cycle with 14 Attack and still 12 Health left. Their swarm has made your boar into their biggest problem.
good_against: WIDE swarms and Peck.
weak_against: One hit big enough to kill it outright, and SCAM kills.

variations.name: Battle-Scarred
variations.text: Scar, but the gains are permanent, up to +5/+5 in total per combat.

variations.name: Thick Skin
variations.text: After this survives a hit, its next hit taken deals 1 less damage.

variations.name: Old Wounds
variations.text: Scar. When this dies, give the unit behind it the stats Scar gave it.

similar_to: Like Hearthstone's Enrage (stronger once damaged), but it grows with every hit instead of switching on once.
designer_response: A payoff for the batch's defensive keywords, so STICKY has something to scale with besides surviving.
open_questions: Does a hit reduced to 0 (Shrug, Curl) count as a hit for Scar? Proposed: no.
source: new, inspired by Hunker, Shell, Shrug and Peck (X) in this batch

rules_review.name: Scar
rules_review.review: Broken: Sounder Matriarch's 'whenever a friendly unit with Scar gains stats, your other Great beasts gain +1 Attack' hits Scarred Boar, a Great beast with Scar, whose gain fires the Matriarch again, without end, until the 10,000-trigger tie (9.10.2). Fix: 'whenever a friendly unit gains stats from Scar'. Scar itself works: 'survives a hit' is checked after that hit's death check, a hit reduced to 0 doesn't count (R1), and the name clashes with Bloodied's Sounder Matriarch (batch 2), a different card.

budget_review.name: Scar

units.name: Scarred Boar
units.estimate: T2 2/5: body 7 + about 1.3 survived hits a fight (its own attacks' retaliation and attacks on it) x +1/+1 this combat x 0.6 realised = 1.6 [guess] = 8.6 vs V(2) 7: +23% (+-15%).

units.name: Old Tusker
units.estimate: T4 4/7: body 11 + about 1.6 survived hits x +2/+2 x 0.6 = 3.8 [guess] = 14.8 vs V(4) 10: +48% (+-15%).

units.name: Sounder Matriarch
units.estimate: T6 5/9: body 14 + own Scar about 2 hits x 2 x 0.6 = 2.4 + about 3.5 Scar gains a fight in a build x +1 Attack to about 3 other Great beasts x 0.5 = 5.2 [guess] = 21.6 vs V(6) 14: +54% (+-15%). If 'gains stats' also counts other buffs on Scar units, more.

budget_review.line: Scar's growth on survived hits is worth more than it looks on tanky bodies, so all three need smaller bodies.

name: Nightfall
label: NEW
group: G. Attack order and timing
summary: An effect that fires when your second round of attacks begins, so the fight has a turning point.
rules: Nightfall: [effect]. When your side's second attack cycle begins (night falls), this effect happens. Once per combat.
bends: 9.4.5: the cycle reset becomes a trigger.
creatures: Moths, owls and other night creatures; Lights glow brighter at night.

units.name: Lamp Moth
units.text: Nightfall: gain +2/+2 for this combat.

units.name: Marsh Light
units.text: Nightfall: deal 2 damage to each enemy back-row unit.

units.name: Glow-worm Lantern
units.text: Nightfall: the units in front of this gain +2 Attack for this combat.

how_they_play: The moths are weak in the first cycle and stronger after night falls. The Glow-worm sits in the back row and lights up the two front units in front of it. The Marsh Light hits the enemy back row just as Nocturnal owls start hunting the weakest, so it sets up their kills.
why_run_it: It rewards units that survive the first cycle, which pairs with protection (Shelter, Thicket) and with Nocturnal.
scene: Turn 4, you have two Lamp Moths behind a Thicket. The hedges soak the first cycle. Night falls: the moths become 3/4s and break the enemy's front row.
good_against: Slow fights and boards that rely on the first cycle.
weak_against: Fast fights that end before night falls.

variations.name: Dawn
variations.text: When your third cycle begins, [effect].

variations.name: Every Night
variations.text: At the start of each of your cycles after the first, [effect].

designer_response: A new trigger inspired by Nocturnal: the owner asked to think about all the game triggers we could use (02f), and the cycle reset is one we haven't used.
open_questions: Does every cycle reset need to be visible in the fight presentation?

rules_review.name: Nightfall
rules_review.review: Works once R4's per-side cycle counter exists: the trigger is the first cycle reset of its own side (9.4.5 step 3). A side that passes should still advance its cycle (R4), or a board of 0-Attack lanterns never reaches night. Readable if the fight shows the moment.

budget_review.name: Nightfall

units.name: Lamp Moth
units.estimate: T1 1/2, back: body 2.75 + '+2/+2 this combat' at night x 0.5 realised x 0.7 alive at night x 1.4 (combat buff on a back unit) = 2.0 [guess] = 4.75 vs V(1) 5: -5%.

units.name: Marsh Light
units.estimate: T3 2/4: body 6 + 2 damage to about 2.5 enemy back units x 0.85 x 0.7 alive at night = 3.0 (E72) [guess] = 9.0 vs V(3) 8: +12.5% (+-15%).

units.name: Glow-worm Lantern
units.estimate: T2 0/4, back: body 4 + '+2 Attack this combat' to about 1.25 surviving units in front at night x 0.8 alive = 2.0 [guess] = 6.0 vs V(2) 7: -14% (+-15%).

budget_review.line: Nightfall is a cheap timed trigger and all three units are in band or close.

name: Close Ranks
label: NEW
group: F. Protection and dodging
summary: When this is attacked, the units beside it also hit back at the attacker.
rules: Close Ranks. When this is attacked, adjacent units with Close Ranks also deal their damage to the attacker at the same time. The attacker hits back only the defender.
bends: 9.6.1: the exchange is no longer one against one, on the defending side.
creatures: Red deer and bison herds that close ranks against a wolf.

units.name: Roe Deer
units.text: Close Ranks.

units.name: Red Deer Stag
units.text: Close Ranks. Adjacent units with Close Ranks have +1 Attack while they join this one's defence.

how_they_play: Line up deer side by side. Each attacker takes damage from the whole line, so small attackers die on contact.
why_run_it: It punishes attacks into a wall of deer, and it rewards placing them next to each other.
scene: Turn 3, you have two Roe Deer in F1 and F2. An enemy 3/3 attacks one: both deer hit it for 2, and it dies.
good_against: Many medium attackers.
weak_against: Gaps in the row, splash and big single hitters.

variations.name: Herd Guard
variations.text: When an adjacent unit is attacked, this also deals its damage to the attacker.

variations.name: Square
variations.text: Close Ranks, and units in front of and behind this join too, not only adjacent ones.

similar_to: The defensive mirror of Swarm.
designer_response: A defensive mirror of Swarm, which the owner liked a lot.
open_questions: Does Close Ranks damage trigger the attacker's Bristle? Proposed: yes.

rules_review.name: Close Ranks
rules_review.review: Works as a defending-side joint strike in the exchange: joiners deal damage at the same time and take none back. The attacker's Bristle pricks each joiner, as proposed, and a Shell attacker hit by several joiners at once falls under Shell's simultaneous-hit ruling. Readable.

budget_review.name: Close Ranks

units.name: Roe Deer
units.estimate: T1 2/2: body 4 + joint defence both ways: about 0.8 times attacked x 0.4 chance of an adjacent Close Ranks partner x 2 x 0.85, twice (it joins and is joined) = 1.1 (E90 joint attack) [guess] = 5.1 vs V(1) 5: +2%.

units.name: Red Deer Stag
units.estimate: T4 4/6: body 10 + partners join its defence (about 1 attack on it x 0.5 x 3 x 0.85 = 1.3) + it joins theirs (about 1 x 0.5 x 4 x 0.85 = 1.7) + '+1 Attack while joining' about 0.4 [guess] = 13.4 vs V(4) 10: +34% (+-15%).

budget_review.line: Close Ranks is cheap without partners; the Tier-4 stag is over on its body plus joint damage.

name: Gall
label: NEW
group: I. Extra bodies, off-slot zones and switching sides
summary: At the start of the fight, this lays a gall on the enemy facing it: that enemy is weaker, and when it dies a wasp hatches for you.
rules: Start of Combat: put a Gall on the enemy unit across from this, or, if that slot is empty, on a random enemy front-row unit. A galled unit has -2 Attack this combat. When it dies, summon a 2/2 Gall Wasp for you into your empty slot nearest this unit's slot (its last slot if it has died).
bends: 8.4: a death on the enemy side summons a unit on your side. Unlike Brood and Changeling, nothing stands on the enemy board, so no new ownership rule is needed.
creatures: Gall wasps lay eggs in oak buds, and the tree grows an oak apple around the larva. Inspired by Brood (34) and Changeling (33).

units.name: Oak Gall Wasp
units.text: Gall.

units.name: Oak-apple Witch
units.text: Start of Combat: put a Gall on the two enemies with the highest Attack.

units.name: Gall Tender
units.text: Your Galls give -3 Attack instead, and Gall Wasps you summon have +2/+2.

how_they_play: Each Gall weakens one enemy and turns its death into a body for you. The Oak-apple Witch aims Galls at the biggest threats. The Gall Tender makes the debuff and the wasps bigger.
why_run_it: It is a debuff and a death payoff in one, and the payoff comes from the enemy's units dying, which happens every fight.
scene: Turn 6. The enemy's 10/10 stands across from your Oak-apple Witch. Start of Combat: the Witch galls it and their next-biggest unit. The 10/10 swings as an 8/10, and when your units finally kill it, a 2/2 Gall Wasp joins your side.
good_against: TALL boards, where one Gall shrinks the main threat.
weak_against: WIDE boards with many small units, where -2 Attack on one token means little.

variations.name: Curse
variations.text: Start of Combat: the enemy across from this has -3 Attack this combat. No wasp. The owner's 'curses that debuff enemy units' for Fairies.

variations.name: Gall Swarm
variations.text: As Gall, and when a Gall Wasp dies, put a Gall on a random enemy unit.

owner_direction: 02h on Fairy curses: "Maybe curses that debuff enemy units is perhaps a better outcome."
designer_response: Gall is a curse that debuffs, with a parasite payoff from Brood's idea, but it keeps everything on your own board.
open_questions: Should Gall be Hive (wasps) or a shared keyword with Fairy curses?
source: new, inspired by Brood (34) and Changeling (33).

rules_review.name: Gall
rules_review.review: Works as a death effect granted to an enemy unit (9.7.2 step 2) whose summon goes to the Gall's controller, so the engine must track who controls a granted effect. Say whether two Galls on one unit stack (two wasps, -4 Attack). Readable.

units.name: Oak Gall Wasp
units.estimate: body 4 + −2 Attack on one enemy this combat (E15 2.2 × 0.8 ≈ 1.8) + a 2/2 Wasp when that enemy dies (3.2 × 0.7 it dies × 0.85 your gap ≈ 1.9) [guess] ≈ 7.7 vs V(2) 7: +10%, ±15%

units.name: Oak-apple Witch
units.estimate: body 8 + Galls on the two highest-Attack enemies (−2 Attack each ≈ 4.4) + two Wasps (≈ 3.8) [guess] ≈ 16.2 vs V(4) 10: +62%, ±15%
units.fix: 2/4, one Gall on the highest-Attack enemy: ≈ 10.1 (+1%).

units.name: Gall Tender
units.estimate: body 9 + −1 more Attack per Gall (≈ 1.5 Galls × 1.1 × 0.6 ≈ 1.0) + Wasps +2/+2 (≈ 1 Wasp a fight × 3.2 × 0.6 ≈ 1.9) [guess] ≈ 11.9 vs V(5) 12: −1%, ±15%

budget_review.line: One Gall per unit is in band; the Witch's double Gall puts two cards' text on one body.

name: Ripen
label: NEW
group: L. Gold over turns
summary: The longer this stays on your board, the more gold it sells for, up to 3 more.
rules: Ripen: this sells for 1 more gold for each of your turns that ended with it on your board, up to 3 more. A unit that is Ripe (3 turns) shows it on the card.
bends: 4.3.3 (sell values are fixed): sell value grows over time. It is a time-bound payoff: keep it and fight with it now, or cash it in later.
creatures: Apples and blackberries ripen on the bough; windfalls in the orchard. Inspired by Cache (47) and the owner's 'take a little now or get more later'.

units.name: Crab Apple Sapling
units.text: Ripen.

units.name: Blackberry Bramble
units.text: Ripen. When this becomes Ripe, give the units next to it +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: Cider Badger
units.text: Whenever you sell a Ripe unit, give your units +1/+1 permanently.

how_they_play: Ripen units fight like normal units while they ripen, then sell for up to 4 gold. The Cider Badger turns each ripe sale into a board-wide buff, so selling them is the plan and not just cash.
why_run_it: It is economy tied to a decision you make every turn: keep the body, or sell it for more than usual.
scene: Turn 2. You play a Crab Apple Sapling in B1. It fights as a 1/3 wall for three turns. On Turn 5 it is Ripe and sells for 4 gold, which pays for the upgrade to Tier 4 a turn early.
good_against: Long, slow games where early units would otherwise be sold for 1.
weak_against: Fast lobbies where you need every slot for stronger units now.

variations.name: Overripe
variations.text: After 4 turns, this rots: it sells for 0 again. Sell it on time.

variations.name: Windfall
variations.text: When this becomes Ripe, get 2 gold and this loses Ripen. No selling needed.

owner_direction: 02h on Acorns: "take a little bit of stuff up front now, or get more later. It always creates interesting decisions." Pillar 13: "Don't move for 3 turns, then X" is good.
designer_response: Ripen is a time-bound payoff in that spirit: the unit keeps fighting while it ripens, so waiting isn't doing nothing.
open_questions: Created units sell for 0. Should Ripen add to that, which would let token makers farm gold?

rules_review.name: Ripen
rules_review.review: Works as a sell-value change, which 4.3.8 allows. Needs a ruling on Created units: 'sells for 1 more' on a 0-value token lets token makers farm gold, so say Ripen adds only to Bought units, or accept it as an economy rule. Say whether a triple keeps the turn count; readable with a counter.

units.name: Crab Apple Sapling
units.estimate: body 4 + up to +3 gold at sale, ≈ 0.8 ripened on average, paid around turns 3–5 when gold moves an upgrade (first gold ≈ 4.5, each further ≈ 1.0: 6.5 × 0.8 ≈ 5.2; E54) [guess] ≈ 9.2 vs V(1) 5: +84%, ±25%. Priced at the Tier-1 table it is ≈ 6.8 (+36%), still over
units.fix: Tier 2 on the same 1/3 (the gold arrives around turns 5–7, ≈ 4.3): ≈ 8.3 (+19%).

units.name: Blackberry Bramble
units.estimate: body 5 + Ripen gold ≈ 4.3 + +1/+1 permanently to its neighbours when Ripe (≈ 1.2 × 2 × 0.9 × 0.8 it ripens ≈ 1.7) [guess] ≈ 11 vs V(2) 7: +57%, ±25%

units.name: Cider Badger
units.estimate: body 8 + +1/+1 to every unit per Ripe sale (≈ 0.3 a turn in a Ripen build × 12 SP × 0.9: s ≈ 3.2, over the Tier-4 cap of 2.5; 3.1 × 3.2 ≈ 10) [guess] ≈ 18 vs V(4) 10: +80%, ±25%
units.fix: 3/3, and the buff goes to your units in this row (≈ 3 units, s ≈ 1.6): ≈ 11 (+10%).

budget_review.line: Three extra gold at sale is a lot at Tiers 1–2, and a team-wide payoff per sale runs over the growth cap.

name: Territory
label: NEW
group: K. Slots, gaps and terrain
summary: This wolf marks its own slot each turn, and enemies that attack whoever stands there get hurt first.
rules: End of Turn: this unit's slot gains 1 Territory (a slot effect, 8.5; it stacks and stays). In combat, whenever an enemy attacks the unit standing in a slot with Territory, the attacker first takes damage equal to that slot's Territory. If that kills it, the attack doesn't happen.
bends: 8.5 slot effects, used for defence. 9.6.1 needs an 'attacker gone' line, as Both Ends does.
creatures: Wolves and foxes scent-mark their own territory. An iteration of Mark (40), aimed at your own ground instead of the enemy's.

units.name: Vixen
units.text: Territory.

units.name: Boundary Wolf
units.text: Territory.

units.name: Old Grey Wolf
units.text: After an enemy dies from Territory damage, give your units +1/+1 this combat.

how_they_play: Each wolf marks the slot it stands in at the end of the turn, so a slot it has held for three turns hurts attackers for 3. You can move the wolf to spread the marks, or keep it still to deepen one slot. The marks stay on the slot, so your next unit there is guarded too.
why_run_it: It punishes every enemy attack into your marked slots and gets stronger the longer you hold your ground.
scene: Turns 1 to 3: your Vixen stands in F2, and F2 reaches Territory 3. Turn 4: you move the Vixen to F3 and play a big unit in F2. In the fight every enemy that attacks your big unit takes 3 first, and the 3/3s die before they can hit.
good_against: WIDE boards of small attackers.
weak_against: Random damage and Start of Combat effects, which aren't attacks.

variations.name: Den
variations.text: Territory only works for units of the marker's tribe.

variations.name: Howl
variations.text: Start of Combat: for each slot with Territory, give the unit there +1 Attack per Territory this combat.

similar_to: Like a defensive Galaxy slot buff.
owner_direction: On Mark: "Mark doesn't make sense to me at all ... Maybe there's iteration to it, but I don't see it right now." (02h)
designer_response: Territory is one iteration: the scent goes on your own slot, as wolves really do it, and it works every fight instead of only against refills.
open_questions: Should Territory have a cap per slot?

rules_review.name: Territory
rules_review.review: Works as a stacking slot effect (8.5) with a pre-strike. Needs the 'attacker gone' line in 9.6.1 (as Both Ends), and a rule for the source of slot damage: with no unit as the source, the attacker's Bristle has nothing to prick. It grows without limit over a game; that is a design dial, not a rules break, and the Rival variation named Territory should be renamed.

budget_review.name: Territory

units.name: Vixen
units.estimate: body 4 + 1 Territory a turn; each point pricks ≈ 1 attack a fight for ≈ 0.85 SP and the slot keeps it (× 1.1): s ≈ 0.95, over the Tier-1 cap of 0.8; 3.9 × 0.95 ≈ 3.7 (E72, E16) [guess] ≈ 7.7 vs V(1) 5: +54%, ±25%. Not linear: once Territory passes an attacker's Health, the slot can't be attacked

units.name: Old Grey Wolf
units.estimate: body 11 + +1/+1 this combat to your units per Territory kill (≈ 0.6 kills a fight in a Territory build × 0.6 × 10 SP × 0.6 realised ≈ 2.2) [guess] ≈ 13.2 vs V(5) 12: +10%, ±15%

budget_review.line: Territory is slot growth that never stops, so its cheap carriers need small bodies, and the sim should find the turn a slot becomes unhittable.

name: Rainbow
label: NEW
group: L. Gold over turns
summary: A fairy starts a pot of gold that grows each turn until you do its task and claim it.
rules: Rainbow: When you play this, a Pot of Gold appears beside your shop. It holds 1 gold and gains 1 gold at the start of each of your turns, up to 10. It has a task. Once the task is done, you may claim the pot at any time in a Recruit Phase: gain its gold, and the pot is gone. You have at most one pot at a time.
bends: 4.1 and 3.2.1: gold held off your hand and board, growing at the start of each turn.
creatures: Fairies and the leprechaun's pot of gold at the rainbow's end.

units.name: Rainbow Sprite
units.text: Rainbow. Task: win 2 fights.

units.name: Cluricaun
units.text: Rainbow. Task: have a Fairy in every back-row slot at End of Turn.

units.name: Gold-Digger Brownie
units.text: After you claim a Pot of Gold, give your Fairies +1 Attack permanently for every 2 gold in it.

how_they_play: The pot grows while you work on the task, and once it's done, waiting a turn is worth 1 more gold. The Brownie turns a big pot into stats too, so a full pot is a board spike as well as gold.
why_run_it: Gold with a goal: it rewards the board you were building anyway.
scene: Turn 3, you play Rainbow Sprite: the pot holds 1. You win on turns 3 and 4; the task is done and the pot holds 3. You leave it, because turn 7 is your big turn. Turn 7 you claim 6 gold, upgrade and buy, and the Brownie gives your Fairies +3 Attack.
good_against: Slow lobbies, where you can let the pot grow.
weak_against: Pressure that forces you to claim early.

variations.name: Rainbow's End
variations.text: "The task is to have a unit at both ends of your front row (F1 and F4) at End of Turn."

variations.name: Chase the Rainbow
variations.text: "Each turn the task moves: it names a random empty slot to fill."

similar_to: Hearthstone's Quests (a task with a reward) and the owner's leprechaun pot of gold.
owner_direction: From 02h on fairy gold: "We could look at some rainbow mechanics, like leprechauns: there's a pot of gold, and you've got to do something to go get it as well ... Just put some more ideas down."
designer_response: A new mechanic built on that suggestion: the pot grows each turn (take a little now or more later) and you must do a task to reach it. Waiting after the task is done is a choice with a cap of 10, in line with pillar 13.
open_questions: Are task wins counted from when the card is played, or across the game?
source: Inspired by Bargain (51) and Wager (50), and the owner's leprechaun idea in 02h.

rules_review.name: Rainbow
rules_review.review: Works as a player-level gold store that grows at start of turn up to 10. Needs rulings: tasks count from when the card is played (proposed), and a second Rainbow played while a pot exists does nothing. Pair's double trigger should still make one pot; readable.

budget_review.name: Rainbow

units.name: Rainbow Sprite
units.estimate: body 4 + a Pot that grows 1 gold a turn to 10, claimed once after 2 wins: about recurring +1 gold for the game, paid in one lump (6.5 × 0.7 ≈ 4.5; E50) [guess] ≈ 8.5 vs V(2) 7: +21%, ±25%. The Pot stays if the Sprite is sold. For information: up to 10 gold in one claim is over the proposed one-off cap (not approved)

units.name: Cluricaun
units.estimate: body 7 + a Pot from turn 6 (≈ 7 gold by turn 12: 4.2 × 0.7 × 0.6 the task is met ≈ 1.8) [guess] ≈ 8.8 vs V(4) 10: −12%, ±25%

units.name: Gold-Digger Brownie
units.estimate: body 6 + +1 Attack per 2 gold to every Fairy when a Pot is claimed (a 6–10 gold Pot gives +3 to +5 Attack × ≈ 2.5 Fairies × 0.9 ≈ 8, once per Pot × 0.6 ≈ 4.8; E01) [guess] ≈ 10.8 vs V(3) 8: +35%, ±15%

budget_review.line: The Pot is about a slow +1 gold a turn and prices near the band; the Brownie's team-wide payoff makes waiting for a full Pot very strong.

name: Offstage
label: NEW
group: N. Waiting off the board: hand and sleep
summary: This card helps your board from your hand, like a prompter in the wings.
rules: Offstage: While this is in your hand, it does its Offstage effect in combat. Only your leftmost Offstage card in hand acts. It doesn't fight and can't be hit.
bends: 3.4.2 (units in hand don't fight and don't count). The hand gains a slot that acts in combat.
creatures: The Folio's fox travelling theatre and Frog Chorus: the prompter offstage.

units.name: Prompter Mouse
units.text: Offstage: Start of Combat: give your F1 unit +2 Attack this combat.

units.name: Wings Toad
units.text: Offstage: after one of your Bog folk dies, give your other Bog folk +1 Attack this combat.

units.name: Stage Manager Fox
units.text: When you play this, give your Offstage card in hand +2/+2 permanently.

how_they_play: Your leftmost Offstage card acts from hand, so you choose which to put first. Playing it later puts a body on the board, so it is a choice each turn: help now or join later. The Stage Manager grows the card in the wings for its debut.
why_run_it: An eighth piece in the fight that can't be killed, at the cost of a hand slot and a body off the board.
scene: Turn 2 you hold Prompter Mouse instead of playing it: your F1 hits for +2 each fight. Turn 6 your board is full, so it stays in hand all game.
good_against: Boards that kill the support units in your back row.
weak_against: Boards that need every body: an Offstage card isn't one.

variations.name: Understudy
variations.text: "Offstage. When a friendly unit dies, this is summoned in its place."

open_questions: Is "leftmost Offstage card only" readable enough, or should Offstage need an empty board slot instead?

rules_review.name: Offstage
rules_review.review: Works with 9.3.1's 'units that trigger from hand' phase. Needs rulings: the snapshot others fight must include your leftmost Offstage card (9.1.1 copies only the board), and the hand needs a fixed order (see Rehearse). The Understudy variation summons from hand in combat, so say the card stays in hand after combat; readable.

budget_review.name: Offstage

units.name: Prompter Mouse
units.estimate: never takes a board slot: Start of Combat +2 Attack to F1 (≈ 2.2) + a slot saved ≈ 1 (E23, proposed E96) [guess] ≈ 3.2 vs V(1) 5: −36%, ±15%

units.name: Wings Toad
units.estimate: +1 Attack this combat to other Bog folk per Bog folk death (≈ 3 buffs a fight × 0.6 realised ≈ 1.8) + a slot saved ≈ 1 [guess] ≈ 2.8 vs V(3) 8: −65%, ±15%; played as a 2/3 it is 5 (−38%)

units.name: Stage Manager Fox
units.estimate: body 8 + +2/+2 to the Offstage card in hand, which counts only if that card is later played (≈ 0.6 × 0.3 × 3.6 ≈ 0.6) [guess] ≈ 8.6 vs V(4) 10: −14%, ±15%

budget_review.line: An Offstage card gives only its effect, so the effect must carry most of a unit's budget; both are written at aura size and come out under. Slot-free value is a guess until simulated.
